title: Fix Flaky Async Tests
question: Debug and fix flaky tests in async message processing. Requirements: 1) Tests fail intermittently (pass 70% of time), 2) Testing Kafka message consumption with @KafkaListener, 3) Test verifies message processed and database updated, 4) Timing issues causing failures, 5) No sleep() allowed in tests. Discuss: using Awaitility for polling with timeout (await().atMost(5, SECONDS).until(() -> database contains expected record)), implementing CountDownLatch in test listener to wait for async completion, using @DirtiesContext to ensure clean state between tests, checking transaction boundaries (@Transactional on listener vs test), using Testcontainers for real Kafka instead of mocks for reliability, implementing idempotent consumers to handle duplicate messages, verifying message ordering with partition keys, using explicit commit instead of auto-commit, and ensuring proper test isolation.

title: Add Tests to Legacy Code Without Breaking
question: Add comprehensive tests to untested legacy codebase. Requirements: 1) Large tightly-coupled classes with static dependencies, 2) No interfaces, direct instantiation everywhere, 3) Database calls scattered throughout business logic, 4) Must refactor to make testable without breaking production, 5) Incremental approach (can't rewrite everything). Discuss: starting with characterization tests (test current behavior, even if buggy), using extract method refactoring to isolate testable units, introducing seams (dependency injection) gradually, creating interfaces for external dependencies, using PowerMock/MockStatic as temporary solution for static calls, applying strangler fig pattern (wrap old code with testable new code), implementing Approval Testing for complex outputs, using code coverage to identify critical paths, refactoring extract-and-override technique, adding integration tests first (safer than units for legacy), and using feature flags for gradual rollout of refactored code.

title: Manage Test Data in Integration Tests
question: Handle test data setup and cleanup in integration tests with real database. Requirements: 1) Tests share database instance (Testcontainers), 2) Tests must be isolated (one test's data shouldn't affect another), 3) Need test data fixtures (users, products, orders), 4) Some tests modify data, some only read, 5) Balance between speed and isolation. Discuss: using @Transactional with rollback for data cleanup, using @DirtiesContext sparingly (slow), implementing @Sql scripts for test data setup, using DBUnit or database-rider for fixtures, implementing test data builders for complex objects, using separate schema per test class, truncating tables in @BeforeEach, using unique test data per test (UUID suffixes), implementing logical deletion instead of physical for safety, caching test containers across test classes, and using @TestMethodOrder for dependent tests only when necessary.

title: Test Service with External API Dependencies
question: Test service that calls external APIs without hitting real endpoints. Requirements: 1) Service calls payment gateway, shipping API, email service, 2) APIs have rate limits and cost money, 3) Need to test error scenarios (timeout, 500, invalid response), 4) Must test retry logic and circuit breaker, 5) Tests should run fast and be reliable. Discuss: using WireMock to stub external APIs, defining request/response mappings for success scenarios, simulating error responses (500, timeout using delayed response), testing retry logic by failing first N requests then succeeding, testing circuit breaker by returning errors until threshold reached, using @AutoConfigureWireMock in Spring Boot, implementing contract tests with Pact for API contracts, recording real API responses for realistic stubs, using VCR pattern to record/replay HTTP interactions, and separating tests (unit with mocks, integration with WireMock, contract tests, smoke tests against staging API).

title: Implement Performance Regression Testing
question: Detect performance regressions in CI/CD pipeline. Requirements: 1) Catch performance degradations before production, 2) Test critical API endpoints (search, checkout), 3) Baseline: search <200ms, checkout <500ms at p95, 4) Run in CI without slowing down pipeline, 5) Alert on regression >20% slower. Discuss: using JMeter in non-GUI mode in CI, defining performance test scenarios (load profiles), setting up baseline metrics (store p95/p99 in database), running tests against docker-composed environment, comparing current run with baseline, failing build if regression threshold exceeded, using Gatling for code-based perf tests, implementing lightweight smoke tests (low load) vs full load tests (nightly), monitoring resource utilization (CPU, memory), generating trend reports, and distinguishing noise from real regression (statistical significance).
